note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following stable low-grade biopsy results and rising PSA trend.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer monitoring. Patient is a 63-year-old retired greenhouse horticulturalist, married, lives alone. Medical history includes hypercholesterolaemia, COPD, and osteoarthritis. Active medications: atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, tiotropium, salbutamol PRN, paracetamol PRN. No known allergies. Social history: non-smoker, alcohol 3 units/week, walks 45 min/day. IPSS score 18/35 indicating moderate LUTS. Hard of hearing, prefers written summaries. Recent appointments: dental biannual check-up, sleep clinic for suspected OSA. PSA trend: 1.8 ng/mL (Jul 2022), 3.0 ng/mL (Nov 2023), 5.3 ng/mL (Feb 2025). Prior biopsies both Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1. No bone pain, haematuria, or weight loss.

On DRE, prostate is smooth, symmetric, non-tender, consistent with cT1c. No nodules or asymmetry palpable. General examination: vitals stable, BMI 21.3, clear lungs, regular heart rhythm. No lymphadenopathy or edema.
